learning: Hypotheses to test: (1) kp 2.0 with weights of ±2 is stable on the oval and s-bend without oscillation; (2) base_speed 1.6 finishes the development tracks under 3 s; (3) last_direction recovers from brief line loss on the slalom. Ask the Race Simulator to report steering_oscillation and line_loss_events so the slalom failure mode is visible.
notes: Iteration 0 integration: baseline symmetric 5-sensor array with a conservative PD-dominant controller (kp 2.0, kd 0.15, ki 0.05), base_speed 1.6, and last_direction line-loss recovery. No race data exists yet, so every value is set from the contract and not tuned.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or integration feedback, so the controller is designed from the simulator contract alone. The geometry is the supplied baseline: five sensors at y=0.04 with x from -0.02 to +0.02 (10 mm spacing), 12 mm footprints, a 0.12 m wheel track and a 0.03 m wheel radius. Sensor weights are set to the sensor x-positions scaled to the [-2, 2] limit, [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]. Because the signal is a reading-weighted average, a line on the left (positive x) gives a positive signal, which steers left, as the contract requires. With 12 mm footprints the signal magnitude stays near 1 when the tape is centred and approaches 2 only when the tape sits under the outermost sensors. Gains: kp = 2.0 gives a turn of about 2 at the outer sensors, roughly 700 PWM of differential, which is moderate. ki = 0.05 is kept small to avoid integral windup on long bends. kd = 0.15 damps oscillation from the 4 cm forward sensor lookahead. base_speed = 1.6 is chosen to cover about 4.5 m in under 3 s (about 1.5 m/s average) with margin for slowing on bends; it is below the saturation point of 2.0 to leave room for steering. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot keeps turning toward the side it last saw the tape when it drops off. Expected result: the robot completes the oval and s-bend at moderate speed; the slalom is the main risk. This is an expectation, not a measurement.
